messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about the performance cycle — dropping questions/notes here so managers and ICs have a single place. I'll answer what I can and add links. :wave:

eli: Thanks! Couple quick ones: 1) If a manager wants to propose an off-cycle promo, what's the minimum evidence needed? 2) How does the comp team handle backdated salary for off-cycle moves?

maria: Great Qs. 1) For off-cycle promos we ask for: short summary of impact, two recent work examples, peer/pm feedback, and a suggested new comp band/target salary. Use the off-cycle packet template (link below). 2) Off-cycle pay is usually effective the next payroll after approval; retro pay is handled case-by-case and requires Finance sign-off.

noah: Template link? Also curious if we can do a mid-month effective date for a hire-promote combo (hire 6/10, promote 7/1) — payroll juggling is my nightmare. :grimacing:

hr-bot: Posted: https://redwood.internal/hr/offcycle-packet (internal only). Attachment: "Off-cycle promo packet + examples" :link:

maria: For hire -> promo combos, we prefer alignments on the 1st when possible. If a manager needs a different cadence, flag it in the packet and Finance will outline the retro calc. Generally we avoid overlapping new-hire onboarding comp changes in the same payroll week unless urgent.

priya: Can you remind us how parental leave / extended medical leave should be documented in calibration packets? We have a teammate who was on leave for Q1 and returned in March.

maria: Please add a "leave context" section in the packet with dates and a short note on expected impact windows. Managers should annotate any goals that were deferred and highlight accomplishments post-return. We explicitly exclude approved leave from negative calibration scoring.

eli: Any updates to the manager comms timeline? Some teams want to schedule 1:1s earlier to give more time for individual discussions.

maria: Updated timeline below — managers can run 1:1s as soon as they acknowledge the comp letters, but final pay changes follow the official schedule to keep payroll predictable.

maria: ```
Updated Spring timeline (high-level):
- May 12-16: Manager calibration sessions (sched by team)
- May 19: Comp letters finalized and sent to managers
- May 20-28: Manager acknowledgement + 1:1s with direct reports
- June 1: Standard effective date for approved promos/comp moves
Off-cycle: case-by-case timing; allow 2-3 weeks for approvals and payroll processing.
```

rebecca: Requesting an anonymized CSV of promotion counts by level last cycle for a leadership ask. Is that something People Ops can post? No PII, just counts and percentages.

maria: Yep — I'll run an export and sanitize it. Expect a post here in ~72 hours. If you need the breakdown by org, say so and I'll include it.

noah: One last logistics Q: if a manager misses the acknowledgement deadline, does that block payroll?

maria: We send reminders and partner with EMs and leads to avoid blocking payroll. If a manager truly misses the window, People Ops will follow up and may apply default actions so pay changes aren't stalled. We aim to minimize exceptions.

eli: Thanks for doing this. Could we have a short office hour for managers tomorrow afternoon to walk through the packet?

maria: Yes — scheduling now. Will post a Zoom + calendar invite in this thread once confirmed. :calendar:

hr-bot: Calendar invite posted: "Manager comp packet office hour" 2026-05-18 16:00 UTC. :spiral_calendar:

maria: Thanks all — I'll add the off-cycle template and the anonymized promo stats when ready. Drop any follow-ups here and I'll triage. :raised_hands:
